the non-radiative transfer of energy to the 4 F 3/2 upper level of Nd 3+ ions in the γ -La 2 S 3 single crystal is realized via a continuous set of trap levels and cross-relaxation from excited states above the 4 F

In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the energy transfer processes in a γ-LaS3 semiconductor single crystals.
the investigation of the processes of population and deexcitation of the 3F3/2 level of Nd3+ in a γ-LaS3 single crystal.
the study of the energy transfer processes of neodymium in the semiconductor single crystal γ-La2S2 and the determination of the energy transfer micror parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the electronic properties of a semiconductor can be modified by the addition of rare earth ions.
the energy transfer micromechanisms of neodymium ions in the γ-La2S single crystal are complex and involve several types of traps and relaxation processes.

the 4F5/2 level of neodymum ions is populated by the nonradiative process of energy transfer from a continuous set (or a single) trap and that the 4G7/2 and 4G9/2 levels are populated by the non-radiative process of energy migration from the 4F7/2 level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy transfer parameters for the La2S3: Nd3+ system are as follows: W1 = 2.3 × 1021 cm-3s-1, W2 = 1.3 × 1018 cm-3s, W3 = 2.5 × 1016 cm-3s and W4 = 1.1 × 1014 cm-3s.

the processes of energy transfer to the 4 F3/2 level of neodymim are determined by a complex set of factors and that the energy transfer microrameters depend strongly on the conditions of the excitation.
the energy of the electronic excita-tion of the 4 F 3 / 2 state of Nd 3 + ions in the La 2 S 3 semiconductor single crystal is mainly transferred to the traps of the crystal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 4F5/2 level is populated through cross-relaxation from excited states located at 0.8 and 1.0 eV above the 4 F3/2 level.
the nonradiative relaxation of the excited states of Nd3+ is due to the presence of a continuous set of energy traps in the crystal.
the energy of the 4f electrons of the rare earths is not only localized in the 4f shell, but also in the 4d and 5d shells.
